question: Which of the following is the oldest mountain range of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aravalli Range.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• With its origins in the Proterozoic era, the **Aravalli Range is the oldest geological feature on Earth.**
 
• It is a** mountain range** in **Northern-Western** India that extends for about **670 kilometres **in a **south-westerly direction**, beginning **close to Delhi,** and going through** Southern Haryana, Rajasthan, and Ahmedabad Gujarat.**
 
• At** 1,722 meters, Guru Shikhar on Mount Abu** is the** highest summit.**
 
• There are **several natural resources** in the **Aravalli Range.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura Range:**

 
 
• Located in the **centre of India**, the Satpura Range is a **group of hills.**
 
• The range begins in** eastern Gujarat **and **extends through Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra's border to Chhattisgarh.**
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• The states of **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu **are all traversed by the **Westen Ghats mountain range.**
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats:**
 
 
• These are a **discontinuous range of mountains** along India's eastern coast.
